milestone_targeted: responds to caregiver's voice; develops social smile
step_by_step_instructions: Choose a familiar lullaby or song.
Hold the baby close and look at their face while singing gently.
Watch the baby's reactions – stilling, blinking, or turning towards you.
Pause and wait for any response, then resume singing.
Repeat the song, varying your tone and pace to keep the baby engaged.

inclusion_modifications.instruction_override: Hearing impairment: hold the baby against your chest so they feel the vibration of your voice (tactile-kinesthetic). Developmental delay: shorten to one repeated phrase and increase the pause time (Navchetana 4.3).

milestone_targeted: develops a social smile; secure attachment
step_by_step_instructions: Hold the baby close to your body with gentle, firm support.
Rock the baby slowly while making soft eye contact.
Talk to the baby in a warm, calm voice and show affectionate facial expressions.
Stroke the baby's back, head, and arms gently.
Celebrate any response – a smile or a coo – with warmth.

inclusion_modifications.instruction_override: Visual impairment: emphasise voice and gentle touch rather than eye contact. Developmental delay: repeat the routine at every feeding and nappy-change opportunity to build predictability (Navchetana 4.3).

milestone_targeted: responds to calming; develops sense of security
step_by_step_instructions: When the baby cries, respond promptly and pick them up.
Cradle the baby in your arms and rock gently in a slow, steady rhythm.
Hum or sing softly near the baby's ear.
Check for hunger, wetness, or discomfort and address any need found.
Continue rocking until the baby is calm, then smile and make eye contact.

inclusion_modifications.instruction_override: Sensory sensitivity: reduce stimulation – dim lights, lower voice, limit rocking to a very gentle sway. Developmental delay: use the same soothing routine every time to build a predictable calming pattern (Navchetana 4.3).

milestone_targeted: raises head; moves arms and legs; body settles with support
step_by_step_instructions: While holding the baby, gently massage their arms and legs.
Try holding the baby upright on your shoulder and gently rub their back.
Try different positions – cradle hold, upright hold, tummy-down on forearm – and notice which calms the baby.
Once you find the baby's favourite pose, use it consistently at fussy times.
Lay the baby on their tummy briefly while you watch and encourage them to lift their head.

inclusion_modifications.instruction_override: Motor disability/low muscle tone: avoid unsupported tummy time; instead hold the baby chest-to-chest so their head is lightly supported. Always supervise tummy time. (Navchetana 4.3)

milestone_targeted: begins to babble; makes sounds other than when crying
step_by_step_instructions: Sit quietly with the baby and listen for any sound they make.
When the baby makes a sound, smile and repeat it back to them.
Pause and wait for the baby to make the sound again.
Show enthusiasm whenever the baby vocalises – widen your eyes and nod.
Keep the exchange going for as long as the baby is interested.

inclusion_modifications.instruction_override: Hearing impairment: imitate the baby's movements and facial expressions instead of sounds – turn it into a facial-mirroring game. Speech delay: accept any mouth movement or breath sound as a 'turn' and mirror it (Navchetana 4.3).

milestone_targeted: attempts to reach and grasp an object
step_by_step_instructions: Choose the baby's favourite toy or a brightly coloured object.
Dangle the toy just within the baby's arm reach to encourage them to stretch out.
Guide the baby's hand gently toward the toy if they need help.
Encourage the baby when they successfully reach out and touch the toy.
Slowly move the toy a little farther to motivate further reaching.
required_materials: baby's favourite toy or bright object

inclusion_modifications.instruction_override: Fine motor difficulty: use a soft spongy ball or clay for the baby to press and hold, improving hand function (Navchetana 4.3). Visual impairment: attach a bell to the toy so the baby reaches toward the sound (auditory cue, VAKT).

milestone_targeted: turns head toward direction of sound; begins to babble
step_by_step_instructions: Hold the baby facing you, at eye level.
Say a simple word or phrase – the baby's name or 'Hello!'
Watch if the baby responds with a sound or movement, then repeat.
Take turns – respond to any noise the baby makes as if it is part of the conversation.
Enjoy the 'conversation'; celebrate every response with a smile.

inclusion_modifications.instruction_override: Hearing impairment: exaggerate lip and facial movements, move close to the baby's face so they can watch your mouth. Visual impairment: rely on voice variation and gentle touch rather than facial cues (Navchetana 4.3).

milestone_targeted: turns head to follow familiar faces or toys visually
step_by_step_instructions: Hold the baby securely and place your finger in front of their face.
Move your finger slowly from one side to the other like a bee flying.
Watch whether the baby's eyes follow the 'bee'.
Move the 'bee' up, down, and in a circle to encourage tracking in all directions.
Repeat the game every day to strengthen visual tracking skills.

inclusion_modifications.instruction_override: Visual impairment: replace with a sound-making toy – move a rattle slowly past each ear so the baby tracks sound instead of sight (auditory-kinesthetic, Navchetana 4.3).

milestone_targeted: looks at and notices new surroundings; turns head toward sounds
step_by_step_instructions: Hold the baby facing outward so they can see the world around them.
Walk slowly around the house or outside, pointing at different things and people.
Name each object or person you show: 'Look – a tree!', 'That is a bird!'
Share simple stories or discoveries about what you see during the walk.
Enjoy a neighbourly walk and talk with baby about the environment.

inclusion_modifications.instruction_override: Visual impairment: describe everything in rich detail – textures, smells, sounds – and let the baby touch safe objects (tactile-auditory, Navchetana 4.3). Motor disability: conduct the walk as a supported lap session indoors, bringing objects to the baby.

milestone_targeted: grasps a toy using all fingers; keeps hands open and relaxed
step_by_step_instructions: Place your clean index finger in the middle of the baby's palm.
Encourage the baby to grip your finger by gently pressing against their fingers.
Allow the baby to hold your finger for a few seconds, then release.
Repeat with the other hand.
Celebrate the baby's achievement with praise and a smile.

inclusion_modifications.instruction_override: Fine motor difficulty: use a soft thin cloth strip instead of your finger so grip effort is reduced. Do not force the hand open – wait for the baby to engage voluntarily (Navchetana 4.3).

milestone_targeted: responds to sensory experiences; social smile
step_by_step_instructions: Gather a few soft scarves, hats, or items of clothing.
Put a hat on your head and say 'Where is Dadi? Here she is!'
Put a soft scarf gently on the baby and then whisk it off playfully.
Use simple language: 'Oh! Where's baby? There baby is!'
Notice and celebrate the baby's laugh or smile.

inclusion_modifications.instruction_override: Sensory sensitivity: use only very soft, lightweight fabrics and keep fabric away from the face. Developmental delay: simplify to just placing and removing a soft cloth from baby's lap before moving toward the face (Navchetana 4.3).

milestone_targeted: laughs aloud or makes squealing sounds; responds to touch
step_by_step_instructions: Lay the baby on their back in a safe, comfortable place.
Gently hold each of the baby's fingers and toes in turn.
Name them using a simple rhyme or song, e.g., 'This little finger…'
Gently wiggle each finger and toe while singing or counting.
Watch the baby's face – laugh together whenever they react with delight.

inclusion_modifications.instruction_override: Hearing impairment: exaggerate facial expressions and mouth the rhyme words clearly so the baby can watch your face. Developmental delay: slow the pace and repeat each line several times (Navchetana 4.3).

milestone_targeted: likes to look at self in mirror; laughs aloud; responds to caregiver
step_by_step_instructions: Choose a short, familiar song or lullaby.
Sing the song to the baby while looking at their face and making eye contact.
Copy the baby's reactions and incorporate them into the song – pause when baby vocalises.
Enjoy the mutual interaction; make it a joyful, shared moment.
Repeat the song every day so the baby begins to anticipate and enjoy it.

inclusion_modifications.instruction_override: Hearing impairment: supplement with bright-coloured picture cards for each verse. Visual impairment: emphasise rich vocal variation – change tone, speed, and volume to keep the baby engaged (Navchetana 4.3).

milestone_targeted: rolls over in both directions; postural control develops
step_by_step_instructions: Place the baby on a soft cloth or in a small hammock with full support.
Gently swing the baby side to side in slow, steady movements.
Encourage the baby to reach out by holding a toy at the side.
Sing or hum along to help the baby feel comfortable and secure.
Stop gently and allow the baby to enjoy the stillness before repeating.

inclusion_modifications.instruction_override: Low muscle tone or motor disability: ensure the baby's head and trunk are fully supported at all times. Reduce swing amplitude. Never leave unattended. (Navchetana 4.3)

milestone_targeted: responds to name; begins to babble with consonants
step_by_step_instructions: Hold the baby face-to-face at a comfortable distance.
Use soft, warm language – share how you feel: 'I love you so much!'
Pause and give the baby time to respond in any way.
Enjoy the connection; repeat encouraging words and facial expressions.
Allow the baby to join in the dialogue through any sounds or movements they make.

inclusion_modifications.instruction_override: Hearing impairment: sign or gesture key words while speaking; let the baby feel the vibration of your voice by placing their hand on your throat gently (tactile-kinesthetic, Navchetana 4.3).

milestone_targeted: oral motor development; imitates facial expressions
step_by_step_instructions: Sit facing the baby at eye level.
Puff your cheeks up with air like a balloon and hold for a moment.
Pop the air out with a fun sound and watch the baby's reaction.
Do it again; wait to see if the baby tries to copy you.
Make various mouth shapes – big smile, round mouth – to encourage imitation.

inclusion_modifications.instruction_override: Hearing impairment: the activity is already visual – emphasise exaggerated face movements. Speech delay: this activity is a core mouth-muscle exercise from Navchetana 4.3 – puckering, smiling widely, and moving the tongue side to side develop the muscles needed for speech.

milestone_targeted: reaches and grasps; rolls toward desired object
step_by_step_instructions: Sit the baby comfortably on the floor with support if needed.
Place a soft, lightweight ball just within arm's reach.
Encourage the baby to reach out and grasp the ball.
Gently roll the ball a little farther to encourage stretching and crawling toward it.
Celebrate each attempt with clapping and praise.

inclusion_modifications.instruction_override: Fine motor difficulty: use soft clay or a spongy ball so the baby can press and hold it easily (Navchetana 4.3). Visual impairment: use a ball with a bell inside so the baby reaches toward the sound.

milestone_targeted: explores objects with hands; shows curiosity about surroundings
step_by_step_instructions: Place the baby in a shallow, safe bath with warm water.
Fill a cup and show the baby how to splash water gently.
Teach the baby to say 'fall' and pour a cup of water into the bath.
Move a small floating toy to show cause and effect.
Name the objects you use: cup, water, splash – and prompt the baby to repeat.

inclusion_modifications.instruction_override: Never leave the baby unattended in water. Motor disability: support the baby's trunk fully throughout. Sensory sensitivity: introduce water gradually – begin with just wetting the hands before progressing to full immersion (Navchetana 4.3).

milestone_targeted: looks for hidden objects; responds to familiar faces
step_by_step_instructions: Open and playfully hide your face using both hands, saying 'Peek-a-Boo! Where am I?'
Reveal your face with a big smile and say 'There I am!'
Open and hide your face in a joyful rhythm to keep the baby engaged.
Wait for the baby's smile or laughter and celebrate with joy.
Encourage the baby to try hiding their own face with your help.

inclusion_modifications.instruction_override: Visual impairment: replace face-hiding with a tactile version – gently place the baby's hand over your nose and then reveal it, saying 'Found it!' Developmental delay: slow the reveal and exaggerate surprise; repeat many times (Navchetana 4.3).

milestone_targeted: tracks moving objects; cause-and-effect awareness
step_by_step_instructions: Hold a plastic or metal bangle and spin it slowly in front of the baby.
Pass the bangle in a circular path at the baby's eye level.
Encourage the baby to reach out and try to grab the bangle when it stops.
Pass the bangle to the baby to explore through touch and sound.
Spin it again and watch the baby's eye movements follow it.

inclusion_modifications.instruction_override: Visual impairment: use a bangle that makes a sound when shaken – the baby tracks by sound. Fine motor difficulty: guide the baby's hand to hold the bangle with full support (Navchetana 4.3).

milestone_targeted: rolls over; crawls to get desired toys
step_by_step_instructions: Place a small clear plastic bottle filled with water or colourful objects on the floor.
Lay the baby on their tummy nearby.
Roll the bottle away from the baby and encourage them to crawl toward it.
Occasionally add small pieces of paper inside the bottle to make it interesting.
Praise the baby when they successfully reach and grasp the bottle.

inclusion_modifications.instruction_override: Motor delay (cannot yet crawl): position the bottle just beside the baby's hand so they succeed in touching it without crawling; gradually increase the distance. Fine motor: use a larger bottle easier to grasp (Navchetana 4.3).

milestone_targeted: uses one or two words; responds to simple requests
step_by_step_instructions: Sit with the baby during feeding time and name each food item.
Smile and respond to the baby every time they look at the food or you.
Encourage the baby to point or reach toward what they want.
Ask simple questions: 'Do you want more?' – wait for any response.
Celebrate the baby's attempts at communication with warmth.

inclusion_modifications.instruction_override: Speech delay: accept pointing or reaching as a valid communicative turn. Use short sentences of 2–3 words. Developmental delay: use the same words every meal to build recognition over time (Navchetana 4.3).

milestone_targeted: object permanence; cause-and-effect understanding
step_by_step_instructions: Sit the baby on a safe surface and place a container and small objects nearby.
Show the baby how to drop an object into the container, saying 'Down!'
Encourage the baby to try on their own.
When the baby drops an object, say 'plop!' together.
Repeat using objects of different shapes, sizes, and textures.
required_materials: any safe object (e.g., ball, crumpled paper)

inclusion_modifications.instruction_override: Ensure all objects are too large to swallow. Fine motor difficulty: use a larger lightweight object and a wide-mouthed container. Visual impairment: use a container that makes a loud sound on impact (Navchetana 4.3).

milestone_targeted: develops fine motor pincer grasp; hand manipulation
step_by_step_instructions: Take a soft handkerchief and tie a loose, simple knot.
Place the knotted handkerchief in front of the baby.
Show the baby how to pull and tug the fabric to loosen the knot.
Guide the baby's hands gently if they need help.
Celebrate enthusiastically when the knot is undone.

inclusion_modifications.instruction_override: Fine motor difficulty: start with a very loose, barely tied knot so minimal force is needed. Gradually make it slightly tighter across sessions. Use a thick soft rope instead of a thin handkerchief if gripping is easier (Navchetana 4.3).

milestone_targeted: uses 1–2 words; recognises familiar people by name
step_by_step_instructions: Sit with the baby and introduce family members one by one using their names.
Say each name clearly – 'This is Dadi', 'This is Papa' – while the person is present.
Ask the baby 'Where is Mama?' and wait for a gesture or glance.
Repeat names consistently every day so the baby associates names with faces.
Celebrate any correct response – pointing, glancing, or saying the name.

inclusion_modifications.instruction_override: Visual impairment: have each family member say their name first, then touch the baby's hand so the baby associates voice with person (auditory-tactile, Navchetana 4.3). Developmental delay: focus on just one or two family members before expanding.

milestone_targeted: understands in/out; develops early spatial reasoning
step_by_step_instructions: Give the baby a box or plastic container and some safe objects.
Show the baby how to put objects in the container, saying 'In!'
Then show how to take them out, saying 'Out!'
Encourage the baby to repeat both actions.
Praise the child when they successfully put an object inside the container.

inclusion_modifications.instruction_override: Fine motor difficulty: use a wide-mouthed container and larger objects that are easier to grip. Visual impairment: use a container that makes a sound when objects land inside (Navchetana 4.3).

milestone_targeted: imitates actions; responds to familiar words with movement
step_by_step_instructions: Choose a short, familiar action rhyme (e.g., 'Chanda Mama', 'Twinkle Twinkle').
Sing each line slowly while performing the matching body action.
Encourage the baby to copy your actions.
Repeat each verse so the baby can anticipate and join in.
Use bright-coloured props if available to make the activity more engaging.

inclusion_modifications.instruction_override: Hearing impairment: add bright-coloured picture cards for each line of the rhyme (visual). Visual impairment: emphasise voice, clapping, and guide the baby's hands through each action (tactile-kinesthetic, Navchetana 4.3).

milestone_targeted: recognises own face; develops self-awareness and body-part vocabulary
step_by_step_instructions: Hold the baby facing you or in front of a mirror.
Point to your own eyes and say 'These are eyes!' then gently point to the baby's eyes.
Do the same for nose, mouth, ears, and chin – name each clearly.
Ask 'Where is baby's nose?' and guide their hand to touch it.
Celebrate every correct response with a warm smile and praise.

inclusion_modifications.instruction_override: Visual impairment: guide the child's hand to feel each facial feature on their own face while naming it (tactile-auditory, Navchetana 4.3). Developmental delay: focus on one feature per session and repeat many times before moving to the next.

milestone_targeted: picks up small objects; self-feeds finger food
step_by_step_instructions: Place a few pieces of child-friendly finger food on a clean surface in front of the child.
Encourage the child to pick up the food and bring it to their mouth.
Observe and respond to the child's attempts; resist doing it for them.
Celebrate each attempt and positive outcome with warmth.
Gradually introduce food of different textures to challenge the child's grip.
required_materials: child-friendly food items (e.g., soft fruit pieces, boiled vegetables)

inclusion_modifications.instruction_override: Fine motor difficulty: use slightly larger pieces so they are easier to grip, or offer food on a spoon with a thick handle. Always supervise to prevent choking. Developmental delay: sit beside the child and guide hand-to-mouth movement using backward chaining (Navchetana 4.3).

milestone_targeted: explores surroundings; identifies familiar objects
step_by_step_instructions: Allow the child to walk or crawl around the house with you beside them.
Point out different things and name them: 'Look – this is a door!'
Let the child touch safe, everyday objects and feel their textures.
Ask 'What is this?' and wait before supplying the answer.
Guide the child away from unsafe areas gently while narrating the space.

inclusion_modifications.instruction_override: Visual impairment: describe the house verbally in as much detail as possible and help the child feel safe objects to stimulate their remaining senses (tactile-auditory, Navchetana 4.3). Motor disability: conduct exploration from a safe seated position, bringing objects to the child.

milestone_targeted: object permanence; searches for hidden objects
step_by_step_instructions: Choose a safe toy the child enjoys and show it to them.
While the child watches, hide the toy under a cloth or behind your back.
Ask 'Where is the toy?' and encourage the child to find it.
Celebrate when the child finds the toy; gradually make hiding places more complex.
Let the child take a turn hiding the toy for you to find.

inclusion_modifications.instruction_override: Non-mobile child: hide the toy in a spot reachable from their position. Visual impairment: use a toy that makes a sound – partially cover it so sound leaks out as a clue. Developmental delay: downgrade to activities for younger children (Navchetana 4.3 Example 1).

milestone_targeted: names and identifies objects in pictures; vocabulary building
step_by_step_instructions: Sit with the child and open a picture book or show colourful picture cards.
Point to each picture and tell the child its name clearly.
Ask the child to point to a picture you name: 'Show me the cat!'
Share stories about the pictures to make the activity engaging.
Encourage the child to turn the pages and choose their favourite pictures.
required_materials: colourful picture cards or picture book

inclusion_modifications.instruction_override: Hearing impairment: use extra-bright, large pictures and point slowly. Visual impairment: replace pictures with real objects the child can touch and feel while you name them (tactile, Navchetana 4.3).

milestone_targeted: imitates actions of caregivers; social turn-taking
step_by_step_instructions: Sit facing the child and perform a simple action – wave, clap, pat your head.
Say what you are doing: 'I'm clapping! Can you clap?'
Pause and wait for the child to copy the action.
Follow the child's lead too – copy whatever action they do and say 'I'm doing what you do!'
Take turns leading so the child experiences both imitating and being imitated.

inclusion_modifications.instruction_override: Non-verbal child: downgrade to a gesture-return version such as 'Hide and Discover' where the child returns gestures instead of speaking, as recommended in Navchetana 4.3 Example 2. Motor disability: choose actions within the child's range of movement.

milestone_targeted: shows empathy; engages in simple pretend care
step_by_step_instructions: Give the child a doll or soft toy.
Show the child how to rock and hug the doll, saying 'Baby is crying – give it a hug!'
Encourage the child to feed, wrap, and soothe the doll.
Narrate what the child is doing: 'You are taking good care of the baby!'
Praise the child for showing kindness and care.

inclusion_modifications.instruction_override: Visual impairment: use a soft toy with distinct texture features. Developmental delay: guide the child's hands through rocking motions first (kinesthetic-tactile, Navchetana 4.3). Accept any caring gesture as success.

milestone_targeted: responds to simple 2-step instructions
step_by_step_instructions: Give the child a simple, clear, one-step command like 'Come here' or 'Sit down.'
Show the child what the instruction means if they seem unsure.
Add a second step once they master the first: 'Pick up the ball and give it to me.'
Celebrate every time they follow the instruction correctly.
Gradually increase the number of steps as the child's comprehension grows.

inclusion_modifications.instruction_override: Hearing impairment: repeat every instruction multiple times while pointing to your mouth; teach the child to lip-read and watch mouth movements (Navchetana 4.3). Developmental delay: break each instruction into one step at a time; demonstrate each step clearly.

milestone_targeted: walks independently; crawls to explore
step_by_step_instructions: Ask the child to close or cover their eyes while you hide somewhere simple.
Encourage the child to walk or crawl to find you.
Celebrate with a big hug when the child finds you.
Take turns – let the child hide while you search.
Gradually choose more complex hiding spots as the child's mobility grows.

inclusion_modifications.instruction_override: Motor delay (cannot walk independently at 14m): downgrade to 'Reaching out to the Ball' or 'In and Out', which require only crawling (Navchetana 4.3 Example 1). Visual impairment: call out periodically 'I'm over here!' so the child can follow your voice.

milestone_targeted: imitates sounds; builds vocabulary of familiar words
step_by_step_instructions: Gather pictures of familiar animals or use household toy animals.
Show the child a picture and make the animal's sound: 'Dog – woof! woof!'
Encourage the child to repeat the sound.
Make corresponding movements too – flap arms for a bird, stomp for an elephant.
Ask 'What sound does the cow make?' and wait for the child's response.

inclusion_modifications.instruction_override: Hearing impairment: use bright pictures of animals and pair each with an exaggerated action (visual-kinesthetic). Visual impairment: focus entirely on sounds and tactile toy animals (auditory-tactile, Navchetana 4.3).

milestone_targeted: develops fine motor skills through play; sensory exploration
step_by_step_instructions: Give the child a small piece of soft dough or clay.
Show them how to roll it, press it flat, and poke holes.
Encourage the child to make simple shapes – a ball, a snake, a flat disc.
Name what they make and celebrate their creativity.
Allow free exploration as the child builds confidence with the material.

inclusion_modifications.instruction_override: Fine motor difficulty: provide wetter, softer dough requiring less force. Guide the child's hands through rolling and pressing (kinesthetic-tactile, Navchetana 4.3). Ensure the child does not put dough in their mouth.

milestone_targeted: names and points to body parts; vocabulary grows
step_by_step_instructions: Sit with the child and ask 'Where is your nose?' while pointing to your own nose.
Wait for the child to point to their nose; help them if needed.
Move through other body parts: eyes, ears, mouth, hands, feet.
Play faster each time, saying 'Touch your ear! Now your tummy!'
Give positive feedback whenever the child correctly identifies a body part.

inclusion_modifications.instruction_override: Hearing impairment: pair each body-part name with a point and touch so the child understands through vision and touch. Visual impairment: guide the child's hand to feel their own body part and name it (tactile-auditory, Navchetana 4.3).

milestone_targeted: uses familiar gestures; participates in group singing
step_by_step_instructions: Sit or stand with the child in a comfortable position.
Choose a song the child already knows and begin singing together.
Encourage the child to sing along with any words they know.
Add hand movements, clapping, or stomping to make it more enjoyable.
Together with others if possible – singing in groups builds togetherness.

inclusion_modifications.instruction_override: Hearing impairment: use a percussion instrument the child can feel vibrating; pair singing with exaggerated movements. Visual impairment: no change needed – this activity is already strongly auditory-kinesthetic (Navchetana 4.3).

milestone_targeted: engages in simple imaginative play; visual curiosity
step_by_step_instructions: Set up a light source shining on a flat wall in a darkened room.
Place your hand between the light and wall to make a shadow animal.
Name the animal and make its sound: 'This is a bird – tweet tweet!'
Encourage the child to wave their hand and make shadows.
Name and describe whatever shadow shapes the child creates.

inclusion_modifications.instruction_override: Visual impairment: replace with tactile puppet play – use puppets made of different textures on the child's hands and give each a distinct voice. Motor disability: the caregiver makes shadows while the child narrates (Navchetana 4.3).

milestone_targeted: understands open/close; cause-and-effect; fine motor manipulation
step_by_step_instructions: Give the child an empty box or jar with a lid.
Show the child how to open and close the container, naming each action.
Encourage them to try on their own.
Place a small surprise inside to motivate the child to open it.
Introduce other containers – zip bags, boxes with flaps – for variety.
required_materials: empty box or jar with a lid

inclusion_modifications.instruction_override: Fine motor difficulty: start with a box that has a loose-fitting lid requiring minimal force. Developmental delay: hand-over-hand guidance to open then immediately reward the discovery inside (Navchetana 4.3).

milestone_targeted: imitates household chores; cooperative play with caregiver
step_by_step_instructions: Take the child to help you sweep a floor area.
Give the child a small broom or let them hold the handle with you.
Ask the child to hold the broom while you sweep together.
Encourage them to try sweeping on their own and guide them lovingly.
Celebrate the finished task together: 'We did it! The floor is clean!'

inclusion_modifications.instruction_override: Motor disability: substitute with wiping a low table with a cloth – seated participation. Developmental delay: break the task into one small step (e.g., only pushing the pile into the dustpan) using backward chaining (Navchetana 4.3).

milestone_targeted: sorts and categorises objects by similarity
step_by_step_instructions: Collect two sets of two or three different items (e.g., two spoons and two cups).
Mix them up in front of the child.
Show the child how to sort them: 'All spoons go here, all cups go there.'
Encourage the child to complete the sorting.
Praise every correct placement and gently correct mistakes together.

inclusion_modifications.instruction_override: Developmental delay: begin with sorting only 2 items of 1 category before introducing a second category. Visual impairment: choose objects with very different textures so sorting is done by touch (tactile, Navchetana 4.3).

milestone_targeted: stacks objects; understands height and balance
step_by_step_instructions: Collect a few plastic cups of similar size.
Show the child how to stack the cups one on top of another.
Encourage the child to build their own tower as tall as possible.
Celebrate when the tower falls: 'Boom! Let's build it again!'
Discuss the tower: 'How many cups? Which is at the top?'

inclusion_modifications.instruction_override: Fine motor difficulty: use wider, heavier cups that are more stable. Developmental delay: begin with stacking only 2 cups successfully before increasing the height (Navchetana 4.3).

milestone_targeted: throws and kicks a ball; gross motor coordination
step_by_step_instructions: Give the child a soft ball or rolled-up pair of socks.
Roll the ball to the child and encourage them to roll it back.
Then throw the ball gently underarm and encourage them to catch it.
Give the ball to the child and encourage them to kick it.
Celebrate every attempt and gradually increase the distance.

inclusion_modifications.instruction_override: Motor disability: substitute throwing with a push along the floor at close range. Visual impairment: use a ball with a bell inside so the child can track by sound (Navchetana 4.3).

milestone_targeted: creative expression through art; colour identification
step_by_step_instructions: Prepare safe colour mixtures using kumkum, haldi, or food colouring in water.
Lay a large sheet of paper on the floor.
Show the child how to dip their palm in colour and press it on the paper.
Encourage them to use both hands and different colours freely.
Let the child explore mixing colours and making different patterns.
required_materials: kumkum, haldi or safe food colouring

inclusion_modifications.instruction_override: Ensure all colouring materials are non-toxic and safe for skin. Supervise to prevent the child from putting hands in their mouth. Sensory sensitivity: start with a small amount of colour on just one finger (Navchetana 4.3).

milestone_targeted: uses 2–3 word sentences; describes objects with adjectives
step_by_step_instructions: Place a few familiar foods in front of the child: biscuit, banana, boiled egg.
Pick up one and describe it: 'This banana is yellow and soft.'
Ask the child to describe another food item.
Introduce taste words: sweet, sour, salty, crunchy.
Ask the child to find all the yellow or round foods on the table.
required_materials: familiar foods (biscuits, boiled eggs, fruit, etc.)

inclusion_modifications.instruction_override: Speech delay: begin with one-word descriptions; use mouth-muscle warm-up exercises (puckering, moving the tongue side to side) before the activity (Navchetana 4.3). Developmental delay: use shorter sentences of 1–2 words.

milestone_targeted: makes 3-word sentences; joins in familiar rhymes
step_by_step_instructions: Choose a short, familiar nursery rhyme the child already knows part of.
Sing it slowly with the child, leaving gaps for them to fill in.
Use hand movements to accompany each line of the rhyme.
Encourage the child to lead the song while you follow.
Repeat the rhyme a number of times so the child gains confidence.

inclusion_modifications.instruction_override: Hearing impairment: pair each verse with a picture card and exaggerated action (visual-kinesthetic). Visual impairment: emphasise rhythm and touch – clap the child's hands with yours on each beat (tactile-auditory, Navchetana 4.3).

milestone_targeted: uses two-word phrases; takes turns in simple conversation
adapted_title: Pretend Play: Talking on the Phone
step_by_step_instructions: Give the child a toy phone or use your hand as a pretend phone.
Model a short conversation: 'Hello! How are you today?'
Pause and encourage the child to respond with words.
Take turns 'calling' each other to build back-and-forth conversation.
Use short sentences and encourage the child to observe your mouth and repeat words slowly.

inclusion_modifications.instruction_override: Non-verbal child: downgrade to a gesture-return activity such as 'Copying Actions' or 'Hide and Discover' where the child returns gestures instead of speaking (Navchetana 4.3 Example 2). Speech delay: practise mouth-muscle exercises before starting; use short 2-word sentences.

milestone_targeted: explores textures; imaginative play with materials
step_by_step_instructions: Fill a container or tray with sand, mud, or rice.
Give the child cups, spoons, and small containers to play with.
Encourage scooping, pouring, and moulding.
Discuss the textures, colours, and feelings: 'Is it wet? Dry? Rough?'
Allow free imaginative play without directing – observe what the child creates.

inclusion_modifications.instruction_override: Sensory sensitivity: offer just a small tray with dry rice first; increase the material and wetness gradually. Visual impairment: the activity is already strongly tactile – describe each texture as the child explores (Navchetana 4.3).

milestone_targeted: moves in rhythm; expresses self through movement
step_by_step_instructions: Put on some familiar music or hum a favourite tune.
Hold the child's hands and move together to the music.
Encourage the child to move their body freely.
Create a simple dance routine together.
Invite other family members to join and make it a joyful group activity.

inclusion_modifications.instruction_override: Hearing impairment: use a drum or tambourine the child can feel vibrating on the floor through their feet; dance to the beat they feel. Motor disability: adapt movements to those within the child's ability – arm swaying while seated is valid (Navchetana 4.3).

milestone_targeted: understands opposites; describes speed of movement
step_by_step_instructions: Explain the words 'fast' and 'slow' using your hands – wave them quickly and then slowly.
Ask the child to clap fast, then slow.
Walk together at a normal pace, then run fast, then creep slow.
Say 'fast' and 'slow' clearly and let the child respond in kind.
Give the child positive encouragement for understanding each opposite.

inclusion_modifications.instruction_override: Hearing impairment: hold up a picture of a running cheetah for 'fast' and a picture of a snail for 'slow' to reinforce the concept visually. Motor disability: use hand movements only – fast and slow clapping (Navchetana 4.3).

milestone_targeted: understands function of objects; uses object names consistently
step_by_step_instructions: Collect 4–5 safe everyday objects: a cup, spoon, brush, cloth, and key.
Hold up each object and ask the child 'What is this for?'
Encourage the child to explain or demonstrate its use.
Name each object and its use yourself if the child is unsure.
Let the child pick an object to teach you about.

inclusion_modifications.instruction_override: Visual impairment: use strongly tactile objects with distinct textures and sizes; guide hands and describe each one verbally (tactile-auditory, Navchetana 4.3). Developmental delay: focus on one object per session.

milestone_targeted: uses hands in creative expression; finger-painting / sculpting
step_by_step_instructions: Take the child outside or use a tray with wet soil or outdoor mud.
Show the child how to press their fingers and palms into the mud to make marks.
Encourage them to draw lines, circles, and shapes freely.
Let the child make 3D shapes – balls, snakes – with the mud.
Allow the child to explore and create without strict direction.

inclusion_modifications.instruction_override: Ensure mud is free from sharp objects or stones. Supervise to prevent the child eating the mud. For children with skin sensitivities: use safe, non-toxic wet sand or dough instead (Navchetana 4.3).

milestone_targeted: imitates household chores; develops responsibility
step_by_step_instructions: Place a pile of clean clothes in front of the child.
Show the child how to fold a simple piece of clothing.
Encourage the child to try folding on their own.
Provide positive encouragement and interactive advice.
Celebrate the finished pile of neatly folded clothes together.

inclusion_modifications.instruction_override: Motor disability: offer the child a small, light cloth to fold rather than heavy items. Developmental delay: use backward chaining – the caregiver does all folds except the last tuck, which the child completes (Navchetana 4.3).

milestone_targeted: identifies shapes; problem-solving; spatial awareness
step_by_step_instructions: Cut a simple picture or drawing into 3–4 large pieces.
Scramble the pieces in front of the child.
Show the child the complete picture first, then ask them to reassemble it.
Give hints if needed: 'Look for the piece with the sky!'
Praise the child at each step and when the puzzle is complete.

inclusion_modifications.instruction_override: Developmental delay: begin with a 2-piece puzzle only. Visual impairment: use puzzle pieces of different textures on each piece so the child can feel which piece fits (tactile, Navchetana 4.3).

milestone_targeted: develops fine motor pincer grip; hand-eye coordination
step_by_step_instructions: Give the child a lace and a few large coloured beads or pasta pieces.
Show the child how to thread a bead onto the lace.
Encourage the child to thread beads one by one.
Celebrate each successful bead; count them together.
Increase the difficulty by using smaller beads as the child's skill improves.

inclusion_modifications.instruction_override: Ensure beads are large enough not to be swallowed. Fine motor difficulty: use even larger beads and a stiff wire instead of string so threading requires less precision (Navchetana 4.3).

milestone_targeted: identifies colours; counts with one-to-one correspondence
step_by_step_instructions: Place 3 small objects in front of the child.
Point to each object as you count aloud together: 'One, two, three!'
Remove one and count again to show the new total.
Ask the child to count on their own.
Repeat the counting exercise using fingers, stones, or toys.

inclusion_modifications.instruction_override: Visual impairment: count using the child's fingers – touch each finger as you count (tactile-auditory, Navchetana 4.3). Developmental delay: begin with counting to 2 and increase slowly over many sessions.

milestone_targeted: observes and learns from peers; social cooperation
step_by_step_instructions: Ask the child 'What can you do on the earth?'
Encourage them to demonstrate an activity they enjoy.
Ask a peer or sibling to show the child something new they can do.
Celebrate both children and encourage them to try something the other showed.
Think about interesting and challenging things you can learn from each other.

inclusion_modifications.instruction_override: Developmental delay: pair the child with a patient, slightly younger or same-age peer so the activity pace matches their ability. Caregiver should facilitate and scaffold the turn-taking (Navchetana 4.3).
